claim: AGRP-expressing neurons are activated during energy deficit and increase appetite and weight-gain.
source: Agouti related protein (AGRP)-expressing neurons are a key hypothalamic population that is activated during energy deficit and increases appetite and weight-gain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about AGRP neurons.

claim: AGRP neurons are considerably more sensitive to energy deficit than POMC neurons.
source: We find that AGRP neurons are considerably more sensitive to energy deficit than POMC neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by differential gene expression data throughout the manuscript.

claim: AGRP and POMC neurons positively and negatively regulate body weight, respectively.
source: AGRP and POMC neurons positively and negatively regulate body weight, respectively (Aponte et al., 2011; Krashes et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Weight loss is accompanied by increased Agrp and Npy gene co-expression in AGRP neurons.
source: Correspondingly, weight loss is accompanied by increased Agrp and Npy gene co-expression in AGRP neurons (Hahn et al., 1998), as well as increased electrical activity (Takahashi and Cone, 2005) and synaptic plasticity (Yang et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: During energy deficit, POMC neurons decrease electrical activity due to inhibitory synaptic input from AGRP neurons.
source: In contrast, during energy deficit, POMC neurons decrease electrical activity due to inhibitory synaptic input from AGRP neurons (Takahashi and Cone, 2005; Atasoy et al., 2012), and Pomc neuropeptide gene expression is reduced (Schwartz et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Nearly all (94.9%) ARC NPY neurons are reported to express Agrp.
source: Nearly all (94.9%) ARCNPY neurons are reported to express Agrp, which is selectively expressed in this brain area (Broberger et al., 1998), therefore we refer to these cells as AGRP neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The transcript Npy was enriched by 432-fold in AGRP neurons over POMC neurons.
source: The transcript Npy was enriched by 432-fold in AGRP neurons over POMC neurons, and Agrp was 252-fold enriched; conversely, Pomc was enriched by 351-fold in POMC neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Agrp was 252-fold enriched in AGRP neurons over POMC neurons.
source: The transcript Npy was enriched by 432-fold in AGRP neurons over POMC neurons, and Agrp was 252-fold enriched; conversely, Pomc was enriched by 351-fold in POMC neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pomc was enriched by 351-fold in POMC neurons over AGRP neurons.
source: The transcript Npy was enriched by 432-fold in AGRP neurons over POMC neurons, and Agrp was 252-fold enriched; conversely, Pomc was enriched by 351-fold in POMC neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The differential expression for non-neuronal markers in AGRP and POMC neuron samples relative to purified samples of non-neuronal cell types was at least 300-fold.
source: The differential expression for these primarily non-neuronal markers in our AGRP and POMC neuron samples relative to purified samples of these non-neuronal cell types was at least 300-fold (range: 318- to 8904-fold), indicating a high level of sample purity (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of marker gene expression data.

claim: AGRP and POMC neurons from fed mice showed 694 differentially expressed genes.
source: The AGRP and POMC neuron cell types from fed mice showed substantial differences, with 694 DEG (Figure 1E and see 'Materials and methods' for criteria).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Agrp was upregulated 4.4-fold in AGRP neurons after food deprivation with q = 3.3e−6.
source: As expected, Agrp (+4.4-fold, q = 3.3e−6 [q-value is false discovery rate-corrected p-value]) and Npy (+3.3-fold, q = 1.5e−7) were upregulated and Pomc expression modestly decreased (−1.6-fold, q = 0.038) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Npy was upregulated 3.3-fold in AGRP neurons after food deprivation with q = 1.5e−7.
source: As expected, Agrp (+4.4-fold, q = 3.3e−6 [q-value is false discovery rate-corrected p-value]) and Npy (+3.3-fold, q = 1.5e−7) were upregulated and Pomc expression modestly decreased (−1.6-fold, q = 0.038) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Pomc expression modestly decreased 1.6-fold after food deprivation with q = 0.038.
source: As expected, Agrp (+4.4-fold, q = 3.3e−6 [q-value is false discovery rate-corrected p-value]) and Npy (+3.3-fold, q = 1.5e−7) were upregulated and Pomc expression modestly decreased (−1.6-fold, q = 0.038) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: AGRP neurons showed 826 differentially expressed genes after food deprivation (51.8% upregulated).
source: AGRP neurons showed 826 DEG after food deprivation (51.8% upregulated), but only 47 genes (46.8% upregulated) for POMC neurons, of which 15 genes were in common between the two cell types (Figure 1C,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: POMC neurons showed only 47 differentially expressed genes after food deprivation (46.8% upregulated).
source: AGRP neurons showed 826 DEG after food deprivation (51.8% upregulated), but only 47 genes (46.8% upregulated) for POMC neurons, of which 15 genes were in common between the two cell types (Figure 1C,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: There is a 17-fold difference in the number of differentially expressed genes between AGRP and POMC neurons after food deprivation.
source: This surprising 17-fold difference in the number of DEG between the two cell types indicates that AGRP neurons are regulated by deprivation states much more strongly than POMC neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on the ratio of DEG counts (826 vs 47) from RNA-Seq analysis.

claim: Cdkn1a is the second-most highly upregulated gene during food deprivation in AGRP neurons (+166-fold, q = 7.7e−7).
source: Here, we find that Cdkn1a is the second-most highly upregulated gene during food deprivation in AGRP neurons (+166-fold, q = 7.7e−7), but it is not significantly changed in POMC neurons (−1.5-fold, q = 0.79), illustrating the importance of cell type-specific neuronal profiling.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Cdkn1a is not significantly changed in POMC neurons after food deprivation (−1.5-fold, q = 0.79).
source: Here, we find that Cdkn1a is the second-most highly upregulated gene during food deprivation in AGRP neurons (+166-fold, q = 7.7e−7), but it is not significantly changed in POMC neurons (−1.5-fold, q = 0.79), illustrating the importance of cell type-specific neuronal profiling.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Cdkn1a expression in AGRP neurons is increased after food deprivation as confirmed by smFISH (p = 1.5e−53).
source: We confirmed increased Cdkn1a expression in AGRP neurons from FD mice by double-label RNA single molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) (p = 1.5e−53, Kolmogorov–Smirnov (ks) test, Figure 1G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH validation data.

claim: Asb4 is strongly down-regulated selectively in POMC neurons from food-deprived mice (POMC: −5.8-fold, q = 2.2e−9; AGRP: +1.1-fold, q = 0.71).
source: Similarly, microarray profiling of the ARC has shown Asb4 was slightly downregulated (−1.25-fold) with food-deprivation (Li et al., 2005), but, with cell type-specific RNA-Seq we find that Asb4 is strongly down-regulated selectively in POMC neurons from FD mice (POMC: −5.8-fold, q = 2.2e−9; AGRP: +1.1-fold, q = 0.71, Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Lepr was upregulated 5.3-fold in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (q = 1.3e−10).
source: Leptin levels fall in energy deficit and this is associated with a concomitant rise in Lepr (+5.3-fold, q = 1.3e−10) in AGRP neurons, as was previously reported for whole-hypothalamus tissue samples (Baskin et al., 1999), but Lepr was not significantly changed in POMC neurons (−1.6-fold, q = 0.39).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Lepr was not significantly changed in POMC neurons after food deprivation (−1.6-fold, q = 0.39).
source: Leptin levels fall in energy deficit and this is associated with a concomitant rise in Lepr (+5.3-fold, q = 1.3e−10) in AGRP neurons, as was previously reported for whole-hypothalamus tissue samples (Baskin et al., 1999), but Lepr was not significantly changed in POMC neurons (−1.6-fold, q = 0.39).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: ER-localized proteins were significantly overrepresented in the group of food-deprivation-regulated genes in AGRP neurons (p = 8.3e−16).
source: ER-localized proteins were significantly overrepresented in the group of food-deprivation-regulated genes in AGRP neurons (p = 8.3e−16, hypergeometric-test), and 95% of these DEG were upregulated (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: 95% of ER-localized differentially expressed genes in AGRP neurons were upregulated after food deprivation.
source: ER-localized proteins were significantly overrepresented in the group of food-deprivation-regulated genes in AGRP neurons (p = 8.3e−16, hypergeometric-test), and 95% of these DEG were upregulated (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: Hspa5 was selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons during food deprivation (AGRP: +3.3-fold, q = 2.5e−10; POMC: −1.2-fold, q = 0.52).
source: A key UPR marker, Hspa5, which encodes the canonical ER-localized unfolded protein-sensing chaperone BiP, was selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons during food deprivation (AGRP: +3.3-fold, q = 2.5e−10; POMC: −1.2-fold, q = 0.52).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: BiP-immunoreactivity was significantly increased by food-deprivation in AGRP neurons (p = 2.5e−42).
source: Correspondingly, BiP-immunoreactivity was significantly increased by food-deprivation in AGRP neurons (p = 2.5e−42, ks-test, Figure 2B,D), indicating UPR activation in AGRP neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: BiP-immunoreactivity was significantly reduced in POMC neurons during food-deprivation (p = 2.5e−19).
source: In contrast, we also found that BiP-immunoreactivity was significantly reduced in POMC neurons during food-deprivation (p = 2.5e−19, ks-test, Figure 2C,D), suggestive of reduced protein translational-load in this population.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Ern1/Ire1 was selectively increased in AGRP neurons by food deprivation (+2.7-fold, q = 0.001).
source: UPR involves a program of gene expression that is regulated by Ern1/Ire1, which was selectively increased in AGRP neurons by food deprivation (+2.7-fold, q = 0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: The fraction of spliced Xbp1 mRNA increased in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation (fed: 7.4 ± 1.0%, FD: 15.6 ± 3.8%, p = 0.043).
source: These RNA-Seq data reveal increased abundance for the Xbp1s spliced mRNA in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation (Xbp1s/Xbp1, fed: 7.4 ± 1.0%, FD: 15.6 ± 3.8%, p = 0.043, one-tailed t-test; Figure 2E), consistent with activation of Ern1/Ire1 endonuclease activity in AGRP neurons after 24-hr food deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis of Xbp1 splicing.

claim: Dnajc3/p58IPK was selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+1.9-fold, q = 0.0007).
source: Two well-established Xbp1s-dependent gene targets (Lee et al., 2003) were selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation: Dnajc3/p58IPK (+1.9-fold, q = 0.0007) and Dnajb9 (+2.2-fold, q = 0.0003).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Dnajb9 was selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.2-fold, q = 0.0003).
source: Two well-established Xbp1s-dependent gene targets (Lee et al., 2003) were selectively upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation: Dnajc3/p58IPK (+1.9-fold, q = 0.0007) and Dnajb9 (+2.2-fold, q = 0.0003).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Atm was downregulated in AGRP neurons with food deprivation (−3.1-fold, q = 7e−5).
source: Atm (−3.1-fold, q = 7e−5), a DNA damage sensing-enzyme that, when reduced leads to increased Xbp1 splicing (He et al., 2009), was downregulated with food deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Elevated stress granule formation was not detected in AGRP neurons from food-deprived mice (p = 0.76).
source: To assess stress granule formation, we used anti-TDP43 immunostaining. Elevated stress granule formation was not detected in AGRP neurons from FD mice (p = 0.76, ks-test, Figure 2F,G), which provides preliminary evidence that Eif2ak3/PERK-mediated translational arrest may not be engaged at this 24-hr food deprivation time-point.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Atf6 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.0-fold, q = 0.0016).
source: An additional signaling arm of the UPR is mediated through the ER-bound protein Atf6 (AGRP: +2.0-fold, q = 0.0016).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Nuclear localization of GFP:ATF6 was not significantly increased in food-deprived vs ad libitum fed mice (p = 0.44).
source: After expression in AGRP neurons, we measured the nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of GFP, which was very low and was not significantly increased in FD vs ad libitum fed mice; whereas the ER-stress-inducer, tunicamycin, strongly increased nuclear localization of GFP in AGRP neurons (fed vs FD: p = 0.44, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) vs tunicamycin: p = 2.9e−16, ks-test, Figure 2H–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP:ATF6 reporter imaging data.

claim: Tunicamycin strongly increased nuclear localization of GFP:ATF6 in AGRP neurons (p = 2.9e−16).
source: After expression in AGRP neurons, we measured the nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of GFP, which was very low and was not significantly increased in FD vs ad libitum fed mice; whereas the ER-stress-inducer, tunicamycin, strongly increased nuclear localization of GFP in AGRP neurons (fed vs FD: p = 0.44, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) vs tunicamycin: p = 2.9e−16, ks-test, Figure 2H–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP:ATF6 reporter imaging data.

claim: Keap1 shows reduced expression with food-deprivation (−2.2-fold, q = 0.05).
source: The transcription factor Nfe2l2 (also called Nrf2) regulates oxidative stress and is normally rapidly degraded in the cytoplasm, in part through association with Keap1 (Kobayashi et al., 2004), which shows reduced expression with food-deprivation (−2.2-fold, q = 0.05).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Gclc was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
source: Nfe2l2/Nrf2 upregulates expression of the key glutathione biosynthetic enzymes Gclc (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002) and Gclm (+1.8-fold, q = 0.002), which are elevated in AGRP neurons with food-deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Gclm was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+1.8-fold, q = 0.002).
source: Nfe2l2/Nrf2 upregulates expression of the key glutathione biosynthetic enzymes Gclc (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002) and Gclm (+1.8-fold, q = 0.002), which are elevated in AGRP neurons with food-deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Mt1 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+34-fold, q = 0.004).
source: Nfe2l2/Nrf2 increases other transcripts associated with oxidative stress, such as Mt1 (+34-fold, q = 0.004), Mt2 (79-fold, q = 0.004), and Srxn1 (+17-fold, q = 1.2e−6), which are among the most strongly upregulated transcripts in AGRP neurons during food-deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Mt2 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+79-fold, q = 0.004).
source: Nfe2l2/Nrf2 increases other transcripts associated with oxidative stress, such as Mt1 (+34-fold, q = 0.004), Mt2 (79-fold, q = 0.004), and Srxn1 (+17-fold, q = 1.2e−6), which are among the most strongly upregulated transcripts in AGRP neurons during food-deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Srxn1 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+17-fold, q = 1.2e−6).
source: Nfe2l2/Nrf2 increases other transcripts associated with oxidative stress, such as Mt1 (+34-fold, q = 0.004), Mt2 (79-fold, q = 0.004), and Srxn1 (+17-fold, q = 1.2e−6), which are among the most strongly upregulated transcripts in AGRP neurons during food-deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Ddit3/Chop was unchanged in AGRP neurons after 24-hr food deprivation.
source: The pro-apoptotic Ddit3 (Chop) is typically upregulated during UPR, however Ddit3/Chop was unchanged in AGRP neurons after 24-hr food deprivation (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: After food-deprivation 9/19 core circadian genes were downregulated in AGRP neurons.
source: We examined the expression levels of 19 core circadian reference genes (Yan et al., 2008; Rey et al., 2011) and found that after food-deprivation 9/19 of these genes were downregulated in AGRP neurons (Bhlhe40 [Dec1], Bhlhe41 [Dec2], Nr1d1 [Rev-erbα], Nr1d2 [Rev-erbβ], Dbp, Hlf, Tef, Per2, and Per3), and only 3/19 were upregulated (Rorb, Nfil3, Per1) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Only 3/19 core circadian genes were upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (Rorb, Nfil3, Per1).
source: We examined the expression levels of 19 core circadian reference genes (Yan et al., 2008; Rey et al., 2011) and found that after food-deprivation 9/19 of these genes were downregulated in AGRP neurons (Bhlhe40 [Dec1], Bhlhe41 [Dec2], Nr1d1 [Rev-erbα], Nr1d2 [Rev-erbβ], Dbp, Hlf, Tef, Per2, and Per3), and only 3/19 were upregulated (Rorb, Nfil3, Per1) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: For POMC neurons, only one circadian transcript was significantly changed (Nr1d2/Rev-erbβ).
source: For POMC neurons, only one transcript was significantly changed (Nr1d2/Rev-erbβ) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: E-box-containing genes were over-represented among differentially expressed transcripts in AGRP neurons (p = 0.00075).
source: E-box-containing genes were over-represented among differentially expressed transcripts in AGRP neurons but not in POMC neurons (p = 0.00075 and 0.31, respectively; hypergeometric-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: E-box-containing genes were not over-represented among differentially expressed transcripts in POMC neurons (p = 0.31).
source: E-box-containing genes were over-represented among differentially expressed transcripts in AGRP neurons but not in POMC neurons (p = 0.00075 and 0.31, respectively; hypergeometric-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: 90% (18/20) of E-box-containing genes that were significantly differentially expressed more than twofold in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation were downregulated.
source: For the E-box-containing genes that were significantly differentially expressed more than twofold in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation, 90% (18/20) were downregulated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Genes encoding proteins that are localized to the synapse were over-represented in the differentially expressed genes from AGRP neurons (p = 1.2e−6).
source: Moreover, genes encoding proteins that are localized to the synapse were over-represented in the DEG (q < 0.05) from AGRP neurons (p = 1.2e−6, hypergeometric-test; Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: Gria3 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+3.4-fold, q = 2e−5).
source: For example, α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and kainate glutamate receptors, which mediate excitatory synaptic transmission, were upregulated in AGRP neurons (Gria3: +3.4-fold, q = 2e−5, Grik1: +3.0-fold, q = 0.03; Grik3: +3.2-fold, q = 0.005), but not in POMC neurons (see Ion Channels, below).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Grik1 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+3.0-fold, q = 0.03).
source: For example, α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and kainate glutamate receptors, which mediate excitatory synaptic transmission, were upregulated in AGRP neurons (Gria3: +3.4-fold, q = 2e−5, Grik1: +3.0-fold, q = 0.03; Grik3: +3.2-fold, q = 0.005), but not in POMC neurons (see Ion Channels, below).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Grik3 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+3.2-fold, q = 0.005).
source: For example, α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and kainate glutamate receptors, which mediate excitatory synaptic transmission, were upregulated in AGRP neurons (Gria3: +3.4-fold, q = 2e−5, Grik1: +3.0-fold, q = 0.03; Grik3: +3.2-fold, q = 0.005), but not in POMC neurons (see Ion Channels, below).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Syndig1 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+8.3-fold, q = 0.008).
source: Food-deprivation also induced upregulation of excitatory synaptogenic genes in AGRP neurons (Syndig1: +8.3-fold, q = 0.008; Syndig1l: +13.2-fold, q = 0.0001) (Kalashnikova et al., 2010; Lovero et al., 2013) as well as kinases (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) that regulate activity-dependent changes in spine morphology and excitatory synaptic plasticity, such as p21-associated kinase 3 (Pak3, +2.0-fold, q = 4e−7), Ptk2b (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002), and Plk2 (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6) (Boda et al., 2004; Seeburg et al., 2008; Bartos et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Syndig1l was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+13.2-fold, q = 0.0001).
source: Food-deprivation also induced upregulation of excitatory synaptogenic genes in AGRP neurons (Syndig1: +8.3-fold, q = 0.008; Syndig1l: +13.2-fold, q = 0.0001) (Kalashnikova et al., 2010; Lovero et al., 2013) as well as kinases (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) that regulate activity-dependent changes in spine morphology and excitatory synaptic plasticity, such as p21-associated kinase 3 (Pak3, +2.0-fold, q = 4e−7), Ptk2b (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002), and Plk2 (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6) (Boda et al., 2004; Seeburg et al., 2008; Bartos et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Pak3 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.0-fold, q = 4e−7).
source: Food-deprivation also induced upregulation of excitatory synaptogenic genes in AGRP neurons (Syndig1: +8.3-fold, q = 0.008; Syndig1l: +13.2-fold, q = 0.0001) (Kalashnikova et al., 2010; Lovero et al., 2013) as well as kinases (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) that regulate activity-dependent changes in spine morphology and excitatory synaptic plasticity, such as p21-associated kinase 3 (Pak3, +2.0-fold, q = 4e−7), Ptk2b (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002), and Plk2 (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6) (Boda et al., 2004; Seeburg et al., 2008; Bartos et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Ptk2b was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
source: Food-deprivation also induced upregulation of excitatory synaptogenic genes in AGRP neurons (Syndig1: +8.3-fold, q = 0.008; Syndig1l: +13.2-fold, q = 0.0001) (Kalashnikova et al., 2010; Lovero et al., 2013) as well as kinases (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) that regulate activity-dependent changes in spine morphology and excitatory synaptic plasticity, such as p21-associated kinase 3 (Pak3, +2.0-fold, q = 4e−7), Ptk2b (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002), and Plk2 (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6) (Boda et al., 2004; Seeburg et al., 2008; Bartos et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Plk2 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6).
source: Food-deprivation also induced upregulation of excitatory synaptogenic genes in AGRP neurons (Syndig1: +8.3-fold, q = 0.008; Syndig1l: +13.2-fold, q = 0.0001) (Kalashnikova et al., 2010; Lovero et al., 2013) as well as kinases (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) that regulate activity-dependent changes in spine morphology and excitatory synaptic plasticity, such as p21-associated kinase 3 (Pak3, +2.0-fold, q = 4e−7), Ptk2b (+31.3-fold, q = 0.0002), and Plk2 (+8-fold, q = 5.2e−6) (Boda et al., 2004; Seeburg et al., 2008; Bartos et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Sv2c was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+5.4-fold, q = 5e−10).
source: GABA signaling is also important in AGRP neurons, and synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (Sv2c, +5.4-fold, q = 5e−10), which regulates the readily releasable pool (Xu and Bajjalieh, 2001) is increased, as is Snap25 (+2.1-fold, p = 1.5e−6), a key SNARE complex component responsible for vesicle fusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Snap25 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.1-fold, p = 1.5e−6).
source: GABA signaling is also important in AGRP neurons, and synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (Sv2c, +5.4-fold, q = 5e−10), which regulates the readily releasable pool (Xu and Bajjalieh, 2001) is increased, as is Snap25 (+2.1-fold, p = 1.5e−6), a key SNARE complex component responsible for vesicle fusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Kcnq3 is downregulated in AGRP neurons with food-deprivation.
source: Previous work has shown transient receptor potential C (TRPC) ion channel subunit expression in POMC neurons (Qiu et al., 2010), which is confirmed by our RNA-Seq data, and we find that an overlapping set of TRPC channels (Trpc1, Trpc3-Trpc7) is also expressed in AGRP neurons (Figure 4A). Moreover, Kcnq3 is downregulated in AGRP neurons with food-deprivation (Figure 4A), as previously reported (Roepke et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and citation to previous literature.

claim: Kcnn3 was sharply reduced in AGRP neurons during food-deprivation (−5.4-fold, q = 0.0006).
source: One of the most striking changes in ion channel gene expression in AGRP neurons during food-deprivation was a sharp reduction of Kcnn3 (also called Sk3, −5.4-fold, q = 0.0006), which is a small conductance calcium-activated potassium channel (SK) that attenuates action potential firing rate during elevated activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Apamin-sensitive SK conductance was absent in AGRP neurons from food-deprived mice.
source: Electrophysiological characterization of AGRP neurons showed the presence of SK-mediated tail currents, confirmed by blockade with the highly selective SK channel antagonist, apamin (Figure 4D). Notably, the apamin-sensitive SK conductance was absent in FD mice (Figure 4G), consistent with reduced Kcnn3 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data.

claim: Apamin blockade of SK channels in AGRP neurons resulted in higher firing rates.
source: Apamin blockade of SK channels in AGRP neurons resulted in higher firing rates (Figure 4E,F), which often elicited bursts and plateau potentials (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data.

claim: AGRP neurons from food-deprived mice were not sensitive to apamin.
source: Similarly, AGRP neurons from FD mice showed a comparable increase in excitability, but in this state the neurons were not sensitive to apamin, consistent with greatly reduced SK-channel expression (Figure 4H,I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data.

claim: For each cell type, many GPCRs were detected at expression levels greater than 20 TPM under either fed or FD conditions (AGRP: 59, POMC: 61, AGRP or POMC: 80).
source: For each cell type, many GPCRs were detected at expression levels greater than 20 transcripts per million (TPM) under either fed or FD conditions (AGRP: 59, POMC: 61, AGRP or POMC: 80) (Figure 5A), which is more than previous estimates of GPCRs for hypothalamic regulation of energy homeostasis (Schioth, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and citation to previous literature.

claim: 8 GPCRs were >10-fold differentially expressed in AGRP neurons compared to POMC neurons.
source: Also, several GPCRs show high differential expression between AGRP and POMC neurons: 8 GPCRs were >10-fold differentially expressed in AGRP neurons and 13 GPCRs were >10-fold overrepresented in POMC neurons (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: 13 GPCRs were >10-fold overrepresented in POMC neurons compared to AGRP neurons.
source: Also, several GPCRs show high differential expression between AGRP and POMC neurons: 8 GPCRs were >10-fold differentially expressed in AGRP neurons and 13 GPCRs were >10-fold overrepresented in POMC neurons (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: GPCR expression was significantly overrepresented in genes that were differentially expressed after food deprivation in AGRP neurons (p = 0.0002).
source: GPCR expression was significantly overrepresented in genes that were differentially expressed after food deprivation in AGRP and POMC neurons (AGRP: p = 0.0002, POMC: p = 3.3e−5, hypergeometric-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: GPCR expression was significantly overrepresented in genes that were differentially expressed after food deprivation in POMC neurons (p = 3.3e−5).
source: GPCR expression was significantly overrepresented in genes that were differentially expressed after food deprivation in AGRP and POMC neurons (AGRP: p = 0.0002, POMC: p = 3.3e−5, hypergeometric-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene annotation enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data.

claim: For AGRP neurons, 13 GPCR genes were >twofold upregulated by food deprivation.
source: For AGRP neurons, 13 genes were >twofold upregulated and 11 genes were >twofold downregulated by food deprivation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: For AGRP neurons, 11 GPCR genes were >twofold downregulated by food deprivation.
source: For AGRP neurons, 13 genes were >twofold upregulated and 11 genes were >twofold downregulated by food deprivation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Hrh3 was reciprocally regulated in AGRP and POMC neurons with food-deprivation (AGRP: −9.5-fold, q = 4.7e−8; POMC: +5.3-fold, q = 0.003).
source: For example, two GPCRs were reciprocally regulated in AGRP and POMC neurons with food-deprivation, most strikingly Gi-protein-coupled Hrh3 (AGRP: −9.5-fold, q = 4.7e−8; POMC: +5.3-fold, q = 0.003; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Gnas was upregulated selectively in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (AGRP: +1.8-fold, q = 0.0002, POMC: −1.1-fold, q = 0.73).
source: Moreover, the Gs subunit Gnas was upregulated selectively in AGRP neurons (AGRP: +1.8-fold, q = 0.0002, POMC: −1.1-fold, q = 0.73).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Gpr6 expression in AGRP neurons increased after food deprivation as confirmed by smFISH (p = 4.8e−10).
source: We extended our RNA-Seq observations by examining Gpr6 expression using quantitative smFISH, which showed a significant increase in the number of Gpr6 transcripts in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (p = 4.8e−10, ks-test, Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH validation data.

claim: Mice with Gpr6 overexpression in AGRP neurons showed significantly elevated body weight compared to control mice.
source: To test the functional consequence of elevated Gpr6 expression in AGRP neurons, we transduced AgrpCre mice with a Cre-dependent virus co-expressing Gpr6 and a fluorescent protein (AGRPGpr6 mice; Figure 5F–H). AGRPGpr6 mice showed significantly elevated body weight compared to mice expressing a fluorescent protein alone (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurement data from viral overexpression experiments.

claim: Nmb was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+8.0-fold, q = 6.0e−5).
source: We also observed increased expression of peptides that are associated with reduced appetite, based on pharmacological experiments: Nmb (+8.0-fold, q = 6.0e−5), Nts (+107-fold, q = 0.0001), Nucb2 (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Nts was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+107-fold, q = 0.0001).
source: We also observed increased expression of peptides that are associated with reduced appetite, based on pharmacological experiments: Nmb (+8.0-fold, q = 6.0e−5), Nts (+107-fold, q = 0.0001), Nucb2 (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Nucb2 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
source: We also observed increased expression of peptides that are associated with reduced appetite, based on pharmacological experiments: Nmb (+8.0-fold, q = 6.0e−5), Nts (+107-fold, q = 0.0001), Nucb2 (+2.3-fold, q = 0.0002).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Nmbr was strongly upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+8.8-fold, q = 0.0008).
source: For example, Nmbr (+8.8-fold, q = 0.0008) and Ntsr1 (+41-fold, q = 0.005) were also strongly upregulated in AGRP neurons, are Gq-coupled receptors, and Nmb has been previously demonstrated to increase AGRP neuron electrical activity (van den Pol et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Ntsr1 was strongly upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+41-fold, q = 0.005).
source: For example, Nmbr (+8.8-fold, q = 0.0008) and Ntsr1 (+41-fold, q = 0.005) were also strongly upregulated in AGRP neurons, are Gq-coupled receptors, and Nmb has been previously demonstrated to increase AGRP neuron electrical activity (van den Pol et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Ccl17 was highly upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+21.6-fold, q = 0.0012).
source: Other genes were upregulated by energy deficit that have not been previously associated with appetite regulation, for example Ccl17 (+21.6-fold, q = 0.0012) and Thbs1 (+12.4-fold, q = 0.0002).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Thbs1 was upregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (+12.4-fold, q = 0.0002).
source: Other genes were upregulated by energy deficit that have not been previously associated with appetite regulation, for example Ccl17 (+21.6-fold, q = 0.0012) and Thbs1 (+12.4-fold, q = 0.0002).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Ccl17 expression in AGRP neurons was confirmed to be upregulated by food deprivation using smFISH (p = 1.4e−20).
source: Assessment of Ccl17 expression using double smFISH in AGRP neurons confirmed food deprivation-induced upregulation (p = 1.4e−20, ks-test, Figure 6C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH validation data.

claim: Microinjection of recombinant CCL17 (500 ng) into the lateral cerebral ventricle elicited a small increase of food intake during the light period (1-hr: p = 0.02, 2-hr: p > 0.05).
source: Microinjection of recombinant CCL17 (500 ng) into the lateral cerebral ventricle elicited a small increase of food intake during the light period (1-hr: p = 0.02, 2-hr: p > 0.05; rank sum-test, Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake measurement data from intracerebroventricular injection experiments.

claim: Chronic viral overexpression of Ccl17 in AGRP neurons resulted in a progressive elevation of weight gain compared to control mice.
source: More strikingly, chronic viral overexpression of Ccl17 and GFP in adult mice by selective expression in AGRP neurons (AGRPCcl17 mice) resulted in a progressive elevation of weight gain compared to mice expressing a fluorescent protein alone (Figure 6J), providing preliminary evidence that CCL17 may play a role in regulating body weight.
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurement data from viral overexpression experiments.

claim: Fgf1 was strongly downregulated in AGRP neurons after food deprivation (−4.1-fold, q = 0.0004).
source: For example, Fgf1, which has been shown to reduce appetite (Sasaki et al., 1991), was strongly downregulated (−4.1-fold, q = 0.0004).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis and citation to previous literature.

claim: Cbln4 was downregulated in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation as confirmed by smFISH (p = 6.8e−17).
source: Based on smFISH, we confirmed that Cbln4 and Bmp3 were downregulated in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation (Cbln4: p = 6.8e−17, Bmp3: p = e −12, ks-test; Figure 7A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH validation data.

claim: Bmp3 was downregulated in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation as confirmed by smFISH (p = 9e−12).
source: Based on smFISH, we confirmed that Cbln4 and Bmp3 were downregulated in AGRP neurons after food-deprivation (Cbln4: p = 6.8e−17, Bmp3: p = e −12, ks-test; Figure 7A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH validation data.

claim: All four tested secreted proteins (PTN, ENPP2, CBLN4, BMP3) significantly reduced food intake over a 24-hr period when delivered by intracerebroventricular injection.
source: To test whether these proteins influence food intake, we delivered them by intracerebroventricular injection. All four proteins significantly reduced food intake over a 24-hr period (Figure 7G), consistent with reduction of their expression levels during food deprivation.
evidence: This claim is supported by food intake measurement data from intracerebroventricular injection experiments.

claim: Differential gene expression in AGRP neurons after food deprivation is considerably greater than has been observed in other cell types after various perturbations of brain state.
source: Differential gene expression in AGRP neurons after food deprivation is also considerably greater than has been observed in other cell types after various perturbations of brain state.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with other studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: RNA-Seq data is available at GEO (accession number GSE68177).
source: RNA-Seq data is available at GEO, accession number GSE68177.
evidence: This is a statement about data availability.
